current.text: The Pelicans roster is crowded, with about eight players who could start, and it is unclear how the 240 minutes will be split.
He and Jeremiah Fears compete for the last starting spot next to Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy, Dejounte Murray and likely Yves Missi.
Experts disagree on whether he starts. The newest preview projects him as a starter, while a Pelicans beat reporter expects Fears to start over him.
Even as a starter, he may play under 27 minutes.
The expert is not a big fan, but sees his ranking area as the right place for late-round steals.
Jamahl Mosley is the new head coach and brings a defense-first identity.
With a March 28 end, the Pelicans play 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks. The expert calls this good.
The Pelicans have a league-high 16 back-to-backs.
Experts see the Pelicans as a weak team. The highest projection is about 34 wins, which would still miss the playoffs.

durable.text: Steals are his one real fantasy category.
He rarely shoots and is not dynamic on offense. He adds little in points, rebounds, threes or assists.
His FG% is low for his position, so he fits teams that punt FG%.
He is not a true floor spacer, even though he once shot about 42% from three.
He is worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: He sits right at the edge of our 144-player draft pool (Yahoo rank 167, ESPN 196, 0 USD value on both sites), so he is a 1 USD final-round steals pick at most. Last season's 5 USD in our league is too much. He mainly fits punt FG% builds that need steals, since his projected 41% FG on about 8 shots hurts and his other counting stats are thin. Early in the season, check whether he starts ahead of Jeremiah Fears and plays more than 27 minutes. If not, leave him on waivers.
